ticket.model_change: External gains RecordlessDestinationPolicy (SOURCE_WITNESSED / NEVER_DISPOSABLE / ALWAYS_DISPOSABLE), the NoRecordOrigin token, and a ROOT tier that starts record-less in Init. That last is what made the defect expressible: Init handed EVERY tier a clone-time baseline -- the state `home clone` leaves behind -- so the one destination an operator actually has was unrepresentable, and a reconciliation that could write nothing into it was indistinguishable from a correct one. DestMovedAt gained the `# NoBaseline` guard the record-write rule already had, because a record that claims nothing cannot have been moved away from. NEVER_DISPOSABLE -- the code as it was -- violates NOTHING, and that is why the axis had to exist rather than a counterexample: safe and useless is not catchable by a safety invariant.
ticket.objective: `home sync --from <project> --to ~/.skill-manager` reported EVERY shared unit held-back -- "no usable materialization record, so its contents cannot be shown to be disposable" -- and exited 0 having reconciled nothing. 6, 7 and 5 units on three real repositories. The same sync against a throwaway root produced by `home clone` succeeds (6 updated, byte-identical), because a clone records baselines and a home that was INSTALLED into has none.
ticket.resolution: A second showing of the baseline rule's first decision, not a second rule. Disposal gains sourceHeldTheseBytes: the SOURCE's own record names the tree the destination is standing on now. The rule is unchanged word for word -- the bytes a fast-forward destroys must be bytes the source passed through -- and only the evidence differs, because a record-less destination cannot answer for itself and the source can. NOT adoption, deliberately. Writing a baseline into the record-less destination asserts that two homes shared bytes they may never have shared, it persists, and the next reconcile in either direction reads it as a licence. Nothing is written; this is a question asked and answered from evidence already on disk, once, per pass. contentDigest and NOT sourceDigest, which is the whole safety argument in one field name: contentDigest is "the bytes this reconcile wrote HERE", so the source demonstrably held them, while sourceDigest is the tree the source was HANDED, which after a merge the source never held. It is also whole-tree, which entryDigests deliberately is not after a merge. Every hazardous shape stays blocked because all of them make the destination hold something else -- a third home's work merged in since, an edit made there, an upstream change -- and each moves the destination's digest off the source's recorded content, routing the unit back to held-back or to a conflict a human resolves. copyUnit was brought under the same value in the same edit, because Disposal is the single reading of the rule and CHM-15 was exactly what happens when it is not.
